end.summary:
Ishita practised naming cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, and sphere.
They distinguished a sphere from a circle using thickness and viewing from different sides.
They identified dice as a cube and a brick as a cuboid using equal sides and square or rectangular faces.
They recognised a cylinder when rotated and identified a cone using its circular base and point.
The open top of a bucket caused confusion when matching an everyday object to a cylinder; no later correction was recorded.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised naming 3D shapes, matching objects to shapes, and recognising shapes when turned or shown in different sizes. They explained the difference between a sphere and a circle, and between a cube and a cuboid, by looking at thickness, faces, and side lengths. The bucket example was confusing because its top is open; this was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, compare a closed cylinder such as a can with a bucket and discuss which features match or differ.
